                25 AUG 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, undertook a series of important review meetings today at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi, focusing on strengthening the implementation of key urban infrastructure and flagship missions of the Ministry. The meetings covered the Gurugram Metro Connectivity Project, AMRUT 2.0 and CITIIS 2.0, with emphasis on expediting implementation, resolving bottlenecks and ensuring that the benefits of these initiatives reach citizens effectively.
Shri Tokhan Sahu chaired a meeting to review the progress and development of the Metro Connectivity from Millennium City Centre, Gurugram to Cyber City, Gurugram, with a spur to Dwarka Expressway, being implemented through Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL). The meeting was convened ahead of the PRAGATI meeting scheduled for the evening, with a focus on assessing the current status of the project, implementation progress and key issues requiring timely resolution.
Shri Praveer Kumar, Joint Secretary, MoHUA, along with senior officials of the Ministry and concerned authorities, briefed the Minister on the latest developments. The officials apprised Shri Sahu of progress on various components, including project implementation, planning and coordination among the agencies concerned.
Shri Sahu stressed the importance of maintaining close coordination among all stakeholders and addressing issues expeditiously to ensure timely progress of the project.
With the officials of AMRUT Division, Shri Sahu assessed the implementation and progress of AMRUT 2.0 and deliberated on the observations made in the 10th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Housing and Urban Affairs.
Smt. Isha Kalia, Joint Secretary, MoHUA, along with senior officials, presented the Ministry's response to the observations and key findings of the Standing Committee Report. During the meeting, officials highlighted that the assessment of AMRUT 2.0 coverage needs to be viewed in the context of the defined scope of the Mission. AMRUT covers 500 cities, with approximately 7.41 crore urban households as per 2025 data reported by these cities. The Standing Committee's assessment, however, has considered data from approximately 4,900 urban cities, covering around 11.32 crore households, which is broader than the Mission's defined coverage.
Based on data reported by AMRUT cities, the Ministry informed that the actual coverage is approximately 55%. It was also clarified that sewerage systems and on-site sanitation systems need not necessarily be treated as mutually exclusive categories, as both can coexist where scientifically planned and implemented according to local requirements.
On sectoral investment, the officials  emphasised that the importance of sewerage and septage infrastructure cannot be assessed merely on the basis of the number of projects. While sewerage and septage projects constitute around 6.8% of the total number of approved projects, they account for approximately ₹71,133 crore out of the total approved project cost of ₹1,97,191 crore, representing nearly 36% of the overall investment under the Mission.
Officials also highlighted that large urban infrastructure projects require substantial implementation time and have long gestation periods. Delays may arise due to factors such as land-related issues, public objections, multiple departmental clearances and No Objection Certificates (NOCs), many of which fall under the jurisdiction of State Governments.
Regarding ongoing sewerage projects, officials informed that 394 projects worth approximately ₹47,230 crore are currently under implementation. Upon completion, these projects are expected to provide new sewerage connections to around 48.76 lakh households, while approximately 60.59 lakh households will benefit through system upgrades and servicing.
Shri Sahu emphasised the need for continued monitoring, close coordination with States and Urban Local Bodies, and timely resolution of implementation bottlenecks to ensure that the objectives of AMRUT 2.0 are achieved effectively. Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Shri Chanchal Kumar, chaired the Conference and interacted with the participating State/UT officials during the deliberations. Referring to the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister, under which India’s soft power and creative economy have been placed among the
Saptdhara,
the seven streams of national progress, the Secretary underlined the need for stronger and more structured cooperation between the Centre and States to harness India’s vast creative potential and strengthen public communication. He said that the creative economy, encompassing culture, creativity and commerce, has the potential to generate employment, attract investment and enhance India’s global influence.
Highlighting the diverse strengths of States and Union Territories, the Secretary said that there cannot be a single model for the growth of the creative economy. He emphasised that the cultural strengths, institutional capabilities and regional talent of every State and Union Territory must be leveraged to realise its creative potential.
He also highlighted areas for enhanced Centre-State collaboration, including infrastructure, ease of doing business, capacity building, regional content and creative ecosystems. National platforms such as
WAVES 2027, WAVES Bazaar, WaveX and the Create in India Challenges
could provide creators and start-ups from across the country greater access to markets, investors, technology and global partnerships.
The participating State and UT officials shared their experiences and concerns regarding the implementation of various initiatives and discussed ways to further strengthen coordination and engagement with the Ministry. The need for capacity building at the State level was also highlighted, with States seeking greater support from the Ministry through enhanced communication, engagement and regular conferences. The officials also expressed their willingness to collaborate more closely with the Ministry and actively participate in strengthening
Orange Economy
.

The Conference also deliberated on a range of issues relating to Public Service Broadcasting, the live events sector, capacity building of DIPR officers, digital transformation in the media & publication sector and public outreach initiatives.
The Secretary also called for closer coordination between PIB Regional Offices, State Information and Public Relations Departments, and regional units of Doordarshan and Akashvani for State-specific content and outreach. He reiterated that the Ministry remains open to new ideas, State-led initiatives and partnership models to strengthen the creative economy and improve public communication.
The Conference saw participation from senior officials of the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, along with I&PR Secretaries and representatives from States and Union Territories across the country, reflecting close coordination and shared commitment between the Centre and the States.

community ownership and Jan Bhagidari

operation and maintenance

73rd Constitutional Amendment

Funds, Functions and Functionaries (3Fs)

JJM 2.0
.

ctive local participation in water system maintenance.

se

user charge of ₹100 per household

title: Parishrama Adalat in Hyderabad resolves 65 delayed-payment cases worth ₹8.29 crore, helping MSEs restore cash flow and business continuity
subtitle: Conciliation and ODR mechanisms help turn delayed payments into renewed business confidence
date:

content:
The ‘Parishrama Adalat’, a Conciliation Conclave for Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) delayed-payment disputes, organised by the Commissionerate of Industries and Commerce, Government of Telangana, in association with the Ministry of MSME, successfully resolved 65 delayed-payment cases involving ₹8.29 crore. Held at FTCCI, Hyderabad, the conclave brought together MSEs, buyers, public sector enterprises, MSE Facilitation Councils, ADR institutions and officials from the Ministry of MSME and the Government of Telangana.
For a Micro or Small Enterprise, a delayed payment is not merely an unpaid invoice. It can affect salaries, purchase of raw materials, repayment of loans and the ability to take up new business opportunities. The Parishrama Adalat highlighted how timely and effective dispute resolution can support business continuity, restore confidence and strengthen commercial relationships.
The strongest evidence at the conclave came from entrepreneurs who shared how delayed-payment resolution affected their businesses and what they were able to do next. These experiences demonstrated that the real impact of dispute resolution is measured not only in cases closed, but in businesses moving forward.
Success Stories: From Delayed Payments to Business Continuity
Recovery of dues restores confidence: Mrs. Shalini of Neemus Software Solutions Pvt. Ltd. described prolonged delayed payments and contract-related disputes that had drained the enterprise’s savings and confidence. Through the delayed-payment mechanism, the enterprise resolved nine out of eleven cases. Her experience highlighted the wider meaning of payment recovery—the restoration of confidence to continue operating and growing.
Conciliation preserves business relationships: Sri Mukund Maheshwari of Nagarjuna Agro Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. shared how intervention by the Council helped clear an outstanding amount from a buyer who had earlier avoided his calls. Beyond recovery of the payment, the commercial relationship survived. He stated at the event, “Cash flow is the oxygen of industry.”
From two years of waiting to resolution in months: Sri Atmakuri Nammalwar of Sree Solutions described waiting for more than two years for dues. Through the dispute-resolution mechanism, the enterprise reported recovery of close to ₹30 lakh, with four cases closed within approximately two to three months.
Inclusive dispute resolution supports every entrepreneur: A case from Karimnagar highlighted the importance of accessible dispute-resolution mechanisms. A person with disability running a home-pipes business was able to pursue resolution of approximately ₹11 lakh in delayed payments. The case underscored the importance of ensuring that the circumstances of an entrepreneur do not become barriers to seeking a remedy.
ODR turns stuck payments into business momentum: Hyderabad Ammonia & Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. faced delayed payments of nearly ₹79 lakh from nine buyers, putting pressure on its cash flow. Through the ODR Platform, three conciliation meetings helped bring the parties together. One major buyer settled ₹20 lakh, while other buyers also began clearing their dues. The company reported recovering ₹54 lakh in total.
Behind every case number is a person: Sri Gopi Krishna of Shabari Industries shared how delayed payments had begun affecting the enterprise’s credit profile. The mechanism helped the enterprise realise approximately ₹40 lakh in two payments. Sri Ranjith Reddy of A.P. Engineering shared that three cases were resolved through ODR, while Sri Srinivasulu of Panduranga Enterprises spoke of a long-delayed matter involving approximately ₹16 lakh that moved towards settlement.
ODR: Bringing Technology, Institutions and Human Intervention Together
The ODR platform, launched in 2025, brings technology into the dispute-resolution process and provides a digital pathway through which delayed-payment matters can be taken forward, while the institutional role of MSE Facilitation Councils remains central to resolution.
Ms. Ankita Pandey, Director, RAMP, Ministry of MSME, traced the evolution of the delayed-payment framework from the Samadhan Portal to the MSME ODR platform. Figures shared during the programme indicated that more than 800 cases had been filed in Telangana through the ODR ecosystem, with around 85 resolved.
Shri J. Nikhil Chakravarthi, Commissioner of Industries, Government of Telangana, placed the initiative within the State’s wider MSME agenda and underlined technology and institutional strengthening as instruments for improving ease of doing business.
The Parishrama Adalat reinforced that the measure of a dispute-resolution system is not simply how many files it processes, but how many businesses it helps move forward. By bringing together conciliation, institutional mechanisms and digital tools, the initiative seeks to reduce the distance between an entrepreneur, a legitimate claim and a possible resolution.

title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy launched Critical Minerals Innovation Hackathon 2026
subtitle: Students, researchers, R&D institutions, start-ups and innovators invited to develop innovative solutions for critical mineral exploration and technology intelligence
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy today launched the Critical Minerals Innovation Hackathon 2026 (CMiH 2026), aimed at strengthening the objectives of the National Critical Mineral Mission by encouraging students, researchers, academic and R&D institutions, start-ups, and innovators to develop innovative technical solutions to identified challenges in the critical minerals.
The hackathon provides a platform for participants to showcase their ideas, receive expert mentorship, and contribute to building a secure and self-reliant critical minerals ecosystem in India. It focuses on two problem statements: Mineral Prospectivity Mapping from Open Data, which involves developing a prospectivity heatmap for lithium or REE pegmatites and validated against known mineral occurrences; and and Smart Technology and Patent Tracker for Critical Minerals to create an intuitive, web-based Smart R&D and Patent Tracking System for critical minerals.
The hackathon will be organized and host by JNARDDC, Nagpur, an autonomous body under the Ministry of Mines, which will serve as the Organising body and Host Institute for CMiH 2026. The last date for idea submission is 20 September 2026, and the winners will be announced during India Mining Week 2026, scheduled from 15–17 November 2026. Two winning teams will be awarded prizes for each problem statement, with the first prize of ₹1.50 lakh and the second prize of ₹1.00 lakh.
Detailed information regarding the Hackathon, problem statements, guidelines and registration is available on the JNARDDC website:
https://jnarddc.gov.in/
The Critical Minerals Innovation Hackathon 2026 marks an important step towards creating an innovation-driven ecosystem for critical minerals and encouraging young minds, researchers and technology innovators to contribute to India's mineral security and technological self-reliance.

The global forum provided an important platform for sharing India’s experiences and learning from international best practices in advancing climate-resilient and inclusive water management.
World Water Week, organized by the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI), is one of the world’s leading platforms for dialogue, collaboration and innovation on water. The annual event brings together governments, development partners, research institutions and practitioners from across the globe to deliberate on emerging water challenges and share knowledge, experiences and solutions.
Representing the Ministry of Rural Development, Ms. Rohini R. Bhajibhakre, Joint Secretary, participated in the session titled “National Initiative on Water Security: Translating National Water Visions to Reality: What Works?” and shared India’s experience in translating its long-term water vision into institutional and operational approaches for strengthening water security at the grassroots level. The session was convened by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and the International Water Management Institute (IWMI).
Highlighting India’s approach, Ms. Bhajibhakre stated that under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, water security has emerged as a key pillar of India’s development journey. India’s Water Vision @2047, aligned with the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, seeks to ensure resilient, inclusive and sustainable water security for all citizens through integrated planning, technological innovation and community participation. Water is increasingly being viewed as a foundation for rural prosperity, public health, women’s empowerment, climate resilience and sustainable development.
The Ministry highlighted that India’s water security framework is being advanced through a combination of flagship initiatives, including the Jal Jeevan Mission and the National Initiative on Water Security (NIWS). While Jal Jeevan Mission is strengthening access to safe drinking water in rural areas, NIWS is reinforcing investments in water conservation, groundwater recharge, water harvesting and other water security-related assets through scientific and data-driven planning.
A key element of India’s approach presented at the forum was the National Initiative on Water Security (NIWS), which prioritizes expenditure on water-related works based on groundwater conditions across blocks. This approach provides a clear framework for directing investments towards water-stressed regions and strengthening long-term water security outcomes through objective and transparent planning mechanisms.
The Ministry further highlighted that the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 places water security among the key focus areas of rural development interventions. The framework promotes convergence between employment generation, livelihood enhancement, natural resource management and creation of durable community assets through participatory planning and implementation.
Technology and Data-driven Planning for Water Security
The Ministry showcased India’s growing use of digital public infrastructure, geospatial technologies and data-driven decision-making for strengthening water security outcomes. Advanced tools such as Yuktdhara - Geospatial Planning Platform, which leverages GIS and remote sensing technologies, support evidence-based planning of rural development and natural resource management interventions. The E-Jal Application facilitates data-driven water budgeting at the Gram Panchayat level by integrating information on water resources, rainfall, groundwater and population.
Capacity building and knowledge dissemination are being strengthened through the E-Saksham Learning Platform, while digital dashboards such as VBGRAMG Soft, SECURE and BhuGRAM enable real-time implementation tracking, financial management, monitoring and transparency across rural development programmes. These technology-enabled systems are helping strengthen decentralized planning and improve the effectiveness of water security interventions across rural India.
The Ministry also emphasized the importance of empowering Gram Panchayats, Village Water and Sanitation Committees and local communities in planning, implementation, operation and maintenance of water-related infrastructure. Community participation, social accountability mechanisms and digital monitoring systems have emerged as important pillars for ensuring transparency, sustainability and long-term impact of rural water investments.

During the discussion, India highlighted the importance of strong political commitment, cooperative federalism, robust digital public infrastructure and community-centered planning in ensuring that investments in water security translate into sustainable outcomes for citizens and communities.
India’s participation in World Water Week 2026 reflects the Ministry of Rural Development’s continued commitment to advancing water security as an integral component of rural development, livelihoods, climate resilience and sustainable management of natural resources. The participation also contributed to the global dialogue on strengthening water security through local planning, technology-enabled governance and community-led action.

It brings together governments, development partners, researchers, practitioners and other stakeholders from around the world to advance knowledge, partnerships and solutions for addressing global water challenges.

title: Study identifies uniqueness of South Asian gut microbiome, critical for lifestyle disease treatment
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
One of the largest and most geographically diverse investigations has found that South Asian gut microbiomes are distinct from those reported in other parts of the world and are shaped by local culture, diet, geography, and lifestyle.
The findings provide an important scientific foundation for developing microbiome-based diagnostics, personalized nutrition, and precision healthcare for South Asian populations, specifically for lifestyle disorders.
South Asia is undergoing rapid urbanization while simultaneously experiencing a sharp increase in obesity, diabetes, and other cardiometabolic disorders. Although urbanization is known to influence the gut microbiome, it was unclear whether these changes occur similarly across diverse South Asian populations.
Until now, most microbiome research has been conducted in European and North American populations, leaving South Asia largely underrepresented despite housing nearly one-fourth of the world's population.
Scientists from Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), an autonomous institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) along with the University of Chicago, and collaborating institutions across India, Sri Lanka, and the USA, designed a study to understand how changing lifestyles influence the gut microbiome across different cultural, dietary, and ecological settings and to generate a comprehensive microbiome resource representing the diversity of South Asia.
Figure 1. Sampling locations across India and Sri Lanka.
They discovered that changes in the gut microbiome of each community follows its own unique microbiome trajectory shaped by local culture, diet, geography, and lifestyle.
Researchers collected stool samples together with dietary, lifestyle, and health information from 575 healthy adults belonging to ten South Asian communities.
Using the South Asian MicroBiome ARray
(
SAMBAR)launched for the first time in India by the scientists of BSIP, the gut microbiomes of 575 adults from ten culturally and geographically distinct communities across India and Sri Lankawe analysed.
The gut microbiome was characterized using high-throughput DNA sequencing of bacterial 16S rRNA genes, followed by advanced bioinformatic analyses. The researchers compared rural and urban individuals within each community and also compared South Asian microbiomes with global datasets.
The project involved a large international collaboration among scientists from India, Sri Lanka, and the United States led by Dr. Niraj Rai, Group Head, Ancient DNA from the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences, Lucknow. Field teams worked closely with local communities across India and Sri Lanka to recruit participants and collect biological samples and lifestyle information.
A community-engaged approach was followed throughout the study, with researchers sharing study findings back with participating communities. Laboratory analyses, DNA sequencing, and computational methods were then used to characterize gut microbial diversity and identify associations with geography, diet, urbanization, and metabolic health.
This approach enabled the team led by Shreya L. Ramachandran, Nagarjuna Pasupuleti, Richard J. Abdill, Niraj Rai and Maanasa Raghavan to identify both community-specific microbial signatures and common microbial changes associated with urbanization and metabolic health.
The study published in the journal Gut Microbes, highlights the importance of including underrepresented populations in global microbiome research. This is the first baseline gut microbiome data from India generated from the healthy individuals in India with huge medical and evolutionary impacts.
By demonstrating that different communities respond differently to urbanization, the study suggests that future microbiome-based therapies should be tailored to regional populations rather than adopting approaches developed solely from Western populations. The SAMBAR resource will also support future research on diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular disease, and other lifestyle disorders that are rapidly increasing across South Asia.

title: New smart technology can make diagnosis of AD more accessible
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A novel smartphone-enabled platform employing afluorescence-responsive tiny molecule as a probe offers a simple, cost-effective, and accessible approach for the detection of the Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarker amyloid-β (Aβ).
Upon interaction with Aβ, the tiny molecule called TZ-48undergoes changes in fluorescence intensity, which are captured and quantified using a dedicated smartphone application. This enables rapid and user-friendly detection, with potential applications in the screening and staging of AD.
AD is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by memory loss, cognitive decline, and behavioural impairment. Central to its pathology is the misfolding and aggregation of amyloid-β (Aβ), which self-assembles into fibrils and deposits as extracellular plaques that trigger neurotoxic cascades leading to synaptic dysfunction and neurodegeneration.
The National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer’s Association (NIA-AA) framework identifies Aβ, tau, and neurodegeneration as core biomarkers for definitive AD diagnosis across brain, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and blood. Importantly, Aβ pathology is an early and AD-specific biomarker, making Aβ a more reliable diagnostic indicator. Although positron emission tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provide valuable diagnostic information, their high cost, need for specialized infrastructure, technical expertise, and limited accessibility restrict widespread use. Blood-based assays targeting Aβ and tau, have emerged as promising alternatives, but are expensive and complex. These limitations highlight the need for simple, sensitive, scalable diagnostic platforms capable of early and accurate detection of Aβ for AD diagnosis.
Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) has emerged as a powerful sensing modality because fluorescence lifetime is largely independent of probe concentration and photobleaching, enabling robust detection of biomarkers and enhancing diagnostic precision.
Scientists at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology, have developed a smart fluorescence lifetime-responsive probe that enables highly selective, sensitive, and differential detection of Aβ fibrils (Aβf) through turn-on fluorescence and distinct lifetime signatures.
The probe called TZ-48 published in the journal ACS Chemical Neuroscience exhibits excellent BBB permeability, robust labelling of Aβ plaques in transgenic AD mouse brains, and compatibility with confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) and FLIM for quantitative mapping of Aβ burden across disease stages. Beyond tissue imaging, TZ-48 enables sensitive detection of Aβ in CSF and blood serum, accurately distinguishing AD from healthy mice.
To facilitate clinical translation, the team of scientists consisting of Krithi K. Bhagavath, Madhu Ramesh, Yogendra Kumar, Sabyasachi Mandal, Hiriyakkanavar Ila and Thimmaiah Govindaraju developed ADxFluor, a smartphone-integrated platform leverages the fluorescence response of TZ-48 for rapid, unbiased quantification of serum Aβ load.
The system combines dual-mode brain imaging, biofluid detection, and smartphone-based quantification of Aβ in biofluids, establishing it along with ADxFluor, a smartphone-integrated platform as a foundation for next-generation smart diagnostics for AD and other neurodegenerative diseases.
The integration of TZ-48 with the smartphone-based ADxFluor platform further establishes a portable, low-cost, and user-friendly point-of-care diagnostic system, representing a significant technological and translational innovation in AD diagnostics.

title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises deeper Integration of Traditional Knowledge with Modern Science and Medicine
subtitle:
Traditional Knowledge Should Move Beyond Conventional Boundaries and Connect with Modern Science, Medicine and Emerging Technologies: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh Visits CSIR-TKDL as Traditional Knowledge Repository Expands Beyond Medicinal Formulations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Traditional knowledge should not remain confined to conventional systems of medicine but should seek deeper integration with Medicine, modern science and emerging technologies to widen its reach and societal impact, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh, said during his visit to the CSIR-"Traditional Knowledge Digital Library" (CSIR-TKDL) here today.
Dr Jitendra Singh emphasised the need for greater outreach and a wider scope of work in the field of traditional knowledge. He said that traditional knowledge should not be viewed only through the prism of Ayurveda and other indigenous systems, but should increasingly be connected with institutions and disciplines across science and medicine as India moves towards a more integrated approach to research and innovation.
The Minister called for stronger collaboration between CSIR-TKDL and academic and medical institutions. He suggested greater scholarly engagement, including opportunities for co-guidance of postgraduate medical students, to expand traditional knowledge research among students and the wider research community. He noted that such collaborations would also help connect the work of TKDL with the younger generation.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also underlined the importance of bringing together cutting-edge technology and India's rich repository of traditional knowledge. He observed that India's advanced scientific and technological capabilities, together with its extensive traditional knowledge base, provide an opportunity to develop a more integrated approach to research and innovation.
During the interaction, the Minister was briefed on the evolution of TKDL from an initiative focused on digitising traditional knowledge into a structured knowledge resource that makes such knowledge accessible and understandable in modern scientific and intellectual property terminology. The initiative was institutionalised in 2001, initially focusing on Ayurveda formulations, and was subsequently expanded to cover other systems of traditional knowledge.
The discussions also highlighted the data architecture and standardised terminology developed for TKDL, enabling effective searches and presentation of traditional knowledge in formats that can be understood by patent examiners. The knowledge resources have been made available to patent offices in multiple languages, including English, French, German, Japanese and Spanish.
The Minister was informed that TKDL has played an important role in preventing the grant of patents based on already documented traditional knowledge. The database has also continued to expand beyond traditional medicinal formulations to cover areas including diagnostic methods, devices and surgical practices.
Dr. Jitendra Singh called for further strengthening the academic and educational outreach of TKDL. He highlighted the need to familiarise younger students and researchers with traditional knowledge, intellectual property and the processes involved in documenting and protecting such knowledge. The interaction also covered ongoing online learning and capacity-building initiatives aimed at widening access to education related to traditional knowledge.
The Minister further emphasised the potential of collaboration between traditional knowledge institutions and organisations working in modern medicine and scientific research. Referring to emerging research and studies involving traditional practices, he stressed the importance of expanding institutional engagement and encouraging evidence-based work that connects traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific approaches.
During the visit, Dr. Jitendra Singh also visited the book stall and digital library, reviewing resources and knowledge collections associated with TKDL. He interacted with officials and experts on the work being undertaken to document, organise and disseminate India's traditional knowledge in a structured digital format.
The Minister also participated in a plantation activity during the visit, reinforcing the broader emphasis on connecting knowledge, science and societal engagement.
The programme was attended by Dr. M. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR; Dr. Viswajanni Sattigari, Head, CSIR-TKDL; and Shri Mahendra Kumar Gupta, Joint Secretary, CSIR, among other officials and experts.
Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed confidence that CSIR-TKDL, by widening its outreach, strengthening interdisciplinary collaborations and connecting traditional knowledge with contemporary science and technology, can further enhance the relevance and impact of India's rich traditional knowledge repository.

Mansukh Mandaviya, Shantanu Thakur Join Sonowal at the National Shipping Board’s Inaugural “SAGAR SAMVAD” in Delhi

content:
The
National Shipping Board (NSB)
held its first ‘Sagar Samvad’ on here today, using the day-long dialogue to press for a five-point roadmap including to add 100 vessels to India's foreign-dependent merchant fleet over the next five years, as expressed by the
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal
during his speech.
The event, themed "Charting the Roadmap Towards Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047," was held at the Civil Services Officers Institute on Vinay Marg and drew senior officials, shipowners, financiers and young cadets from India's maritime training institutes. Sagar Samvad, which means "ocean dialogue," carries the board's motto as its theme line: "Wisdom in the Ocean, Progress in the Nation.”
The inaugural edition of Sagar Samvad was chaired by Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal, who launched the board's first official website. NSB Chairperson Sameer Kumar Khare used the session to submit the board's annual report for 2025-26, subcommittee reports containing the policy advice for the government to Sonowal, outlining the board's work since its reconstitution in May 2025.
"The National Shipping Board (NSB) is older than the ministry it advises
, a
statutory body constituted in 1958 with one job: make sure India's shipping policy is written only after listening to the people who sail it, own it and pay for it,"
Sarbananda Sonowal
said. “Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister
Narendra Modi
,
under the re-enacted Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, and the new National Shipping Board Rules, the mandate has been renewed and strengthened. That is exactly why a platform like ‘Sagar Samvad’ matters
,
bringing policymakers, industry captains, technocrats and civil society into one room to argue, test ideas and build intellectual consensus in the open as per the highest tradition of a thriving democracy like India. That consensus, and nothing else, is what will carry us to an Atmanirbhar Shipping Bharat by 2047.”
Also in attendance was Vijay Kumar, Secretary of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Sonowal held a special interaction with trainee officers from maritime training institutes, taking questions from what organisers called the sector's "Yuva Shakti," or youth power. Sonowal also acknowledged the success
of the Container
Manufacturing Assistance Scheme, worth ₹10,000 crore, with global shipping major
Maersk now
ordering containers built on Indian soil.
"I welcome the National Shipping Board's five-point roadmap
,
fiscal reform, assured cargo support, access to competitive financing, regulatory streamlining and a genuine ease of doing business,"
Sarbananda Sonowal
said. "Taken together, these are not five separate
tasks
; they are the architecture of a nation choosing, at last, to own its own trade. Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister
Narendra Modi, we are quadrupling our port capacity to 10,000 million tonnes a year by 2047. NSB's task is to ensure Indian shipowners stand inside that growth
,
not watching it sail past on someone else's deck.”
Later in the day, a session on "Maritime Labour Force
:
Opportunities and Challenges" was chaired by
Union Minister of Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Mansukh Mandaviya
. The session took up the state of India's seafaring workforce, among the largest in the world, against the board's own findings on wage taxation, pension gaps and welfare provisions facing Indian seafarers, tying the government's youth and labour policy directly to the country's maritime ambitions.
Speaking
at the
session,
Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya
said, “India’s maritime sector has the potential to become a major engine of employment for our young workforce and position India as the world’s leading supplier of skilled seafarers. Under the leadership of our dynamic Prime Minister
Narendra Mod
i,
we are expanding quality training capacity, with steps taken to strengthen industry-led skilling, create wider employment pathways, address gender disparity and equip our workforce with skills for emerging segments such as cruise shipping and advanced shipbuilding. A skilled and future-ready maritime workforce will be central to achieving our Maritime India Vision 2030 and building India’s shipbuilding capabilities under Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.”
Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya
emphasised that India must leverage the expanding global demand for skilled maritime professionals to create high-quality employment opportunities for its growing youth population. He called for coordinated efforts among the government, maritime industry, trade bodies and training institutions to expand training capacity, strengthen market outreach for Indian seafarers and build future-ready skills. He also emphasised the need to address gender disparity in maritime employment, develop specialised talent for emerging segments such as cruise shipping and create a skilled workforce capable of supporting India's ambition to become one of the world's leading shipbuilding nations.
The
Union Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Shantanu Thakur
presided over a panel discussion titled "Augmentation of Indian Tonnage: Opportunities and Challenges.”
"India pays close to $75 billion every year in freight to foreign shipping lines, to move cargo as critical as our crude oil, our gas, our coal and our urea,"
Shantanu Thakur
said. "That is not a performance problem for Indian shipowners
,
it is a competitiveness and demand-partnership problem. For India to become a
Viksit
Bharat by 2047, we cannot depend on the goodwill of others to secure our own trade routes. We must command our own waterline.”
The  session also featured addresses by Capt. M.P. Basin and C.V. Subbarao. The valedictory panel on tonnage augmentation saw Atul Jadhav, Vice-President of the Indian Maritime Foundation; Anil Devli, Chief Executive Officer of the Indian National Shipowners' Association and an NSB member; Capt. S.I.A.K. Azad, Nautical Adviser at the DGMA; Ashutosh Sharma, Chief General Manager at the International Financial Services Centres Authority in Gandhinagar; Rahul Modi, President of the Container Shipping Lines Association and an NSB member; and Capt. Pankaj Kumar, Managing Director of Diamond Blue Shipping Solutions.
Panelists said flying the Indian flag remains 16% to 20% costlier than operating under a foreign one, a gap they attributed to India's tax on ship imports and maintenance services, tax deducted at seafarers' wages, tax on freight and higher domestic capital costs
,
expenses foreign competitors do not carry. Yet under the sector's Right of First Refusal mechanism, Indian owners are still expected to match foreign freight rates to win cargo, the panel said.
The panel proposed a five-pillar roadmap: fiscal reform, assured cargo support, access to competitive financing, regulatory streamlining and improved ease of doing business (EODB). The measures, if adopted, could help India add 100 ships to its fleet within five years
,
a step toward the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision, or MAKV, 2047 target of ranking among the world's top five ship owning nations, the panel argued.
In his welcome speech,
NSB Chairperson, Sameer Kumar Khare
said, “This entire effort draws inspiration from the vision of our Prime Minister, who has placed the Blue Economy at the centre of Viksit Bharat under the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. Under the decisive leadership of Shri Sarbananda Sonowal
,
that vision has translated into high-impact infrastructure, port modernisation, and green shipping reforms on the ground.”
The National Shipping Board (NSB) is a statutory advisory body under the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, that counsels the government on shipping policy, tonnage, seafarer welfare and port-linked maritime development.
The inaugural edition of ‘Sagar Samvad’ programme of NSB brought together maritime stakeholders, industry representatives and experts across three sessions, with discussions centred on the roadmap for Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.
One
of the
sessions
focused on “Maritime Labour Force
:
Opportunities & Challenges”, covering employment generation, seafarer skills, workforce development and emerging opportunities in the sector. Another session, “Augmentation of Indian Tonnage
:
Opportunities & Challenges”, examined the need to expand India’s shipping fleet and strengthen the country’s maritime capacity. The deliberations provided a platform for industry and stakeholders to share perspectives on building a stronger, more competitive and future-ready Indian maritime sector.

title: From Homemaker To Driving School Entrepreneur: How NBCFDC Support Empowered Wayanad Kerala Based OBC Ezhava Community Woman Mini Devi
date:

                25 AUG 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Access to affordable finance can enable women to turn practical ideas into sustainable enterprises. Timely credit support helps aspiring entrepreneurs overcome capital constraints, build livelihoods and create services that benefit their communities.
Mini Devi, a resident of Wayanad district in Kerala, has experienced this transformation through self-employment assistance provided by the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC)
through the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC).
A member of the OBC Ezhava community, Mini Devi was a homemaker who depended on household income. She wanted to become financially independent and establish an enterprise of her own, but limited resources prevented her from taking the first step.
Mini Devi aspired to start a driving school that would offer a comfortable and supportive learning environment, particularly for women. She also wanted to help women acquire driving skills, improve their mobility and become more confident and self-reliant.
The principal barrier was economic. Establishing a driving school required capital to purchase a training vehicle and create suitable office and classroom facilities. Without sufficient savings or an independent income, Mini Devi was unable to make the necessary investment.
With the loan, Mini Devi purchased a training vehicle and established an office for her venture, Malanad Driving School. The support enabled her to create the essential infrastructure required to begin operations and serve learners in her area.
Mini Devi’s women-friendly approach provides learners with a supportive setting in which they can acquire driving skills with confidence and convenience.
Today, Mini Devi is a confident entrepreneur and the owner of a successful driving school. Her transition from homemaker to business owner has brought financial independence, greater self-confidence and a stronger role in her family and community.
Mini Devi’s journey demonstrates how affordable credit and institutional support can help women overcome economic barriers and build viable enterprises. Her success also extends beyond personal income by enabling other women to gain mobility, skills and independence.
Talking about impact of the support, Mini Devi said,
“I received an individual self-employment loan of Rs 3 lakh from NBCFDC through KSBCDC in 2025 that proved a turning point to translate my entrepreneurial vision into reality. I now successfully manage the driving school with a special focus on training women learners. After receiving the loan, my income increased to approximately Rs 40,000 per month strengthening my financial position and reducing dependence on household income.”
Through determination and timely assistance from NBCFDC through KSBCDC, Mini Devi transformed her aspiration into a sustainable livelihood. Malanad Driving School stands as an inspiring example of women-led entrepreneurship and the wider social impact of targeted self-employment support.

title: From Financial Constraints to a Doctorate: How NFSC Support Empowered Vaishnavi’s Academic Journey

content:
For scholars from financially constrained families, meeting the cost of advanced education can be difficult. Timely fellowship assistance can reduce this burden and allow scholars to pursue their academic ambitions with greater confidence and peace of mind.
Demonstrating the impact of support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Vaishnavi, a 29-year-old scholar from Bengaluru, Karnataka,
overcame financial constraints to complete her Ph.D. and earn a doctorate degree.
Before receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme, Vaishnavi’s primary challenge was financial. Although she did not face educational, social, geographical, accessibility-related or occupational barriers, it was difficult for her family to pay the fees required for her higher education.

title: From Outsourced Sewer Work to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneurship: How NAMASTE–SUY Transformed Sushil Kumar Sharma’s Livelihood
date:

                25 AUG 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Mechanisation and access to affordable finance can transform sanitation work into safer, dignified and sustainable self-employment. Timely assistance enables experienced workers to acquire modern equipment, improve service delivery and secure a more stable livelihood.
Sushil Kumar Sharma, a 32-year-old resident of Ward No. 23 near Loyalka School, Rajura, Pilani, in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan, has experienced this transformation through the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY)
under the NAMASTE initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.
A graduate with a Bachelor of Arts degree, Sushil belongs to a modest family and lives with his elderly parents. He is the principal earning member of the household. He has also fulfilled his responsibilities towards his three sisters, who are now married. His father’s poor health and the family’s difficult financial circumstances compelled Sushil to discontinue his studies and begin working to support the household. He later joined Nagar Palika Vidya Vihar, Pilani, as an outsourced sewer-cleaning worker and earned approximately ₹15,000 per month.
The work was physically demanding and offered limited financial security. Sushil faced unstable employment, occupational hardship, restricted access to capital and the social stigma associated with sanitation work. Despite these challenges, he remained committed to supporting his family and aspired to establish dignified self-employment in sanitation services.
Sushil received assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana within the NAMASTE framework. The support enabled him to procure a tractor with a suction tanker for mechanised sewer and septic-tank cleaning services.
The project, supported on 15 January 2026, had a total cost of ₹
10.70 lakh. It was financed through a loan of
₹
5.35 lakh and a capital subsidy of
₹
5.35 lakh.
Access to the vehicle and equipment enabled Sushil to move beyond outsourced work and establish himself as a self-employed sanitation entrepreneur.
Mechanisation made sanitation operations more efficient and reduced dependence on physically strenuous cleaning practices. It also gave Sushil greater control over his work and created a more stable and dignified source of livelihood.
Expressing his contentment over help and support through NAMASTE–SUY,
Sushil Kumar Sharma said,
“My monthly income increased from approximately ₹
15,000 to
₹
30,000
–
₹
35,000. The improved earnings have strengthened my financial position and enabled me to support elderly parents and meet the family
’
s needs with greater confidence”.
Today, Sushil is the owner and operator of a mechanised sanitation enterprise. His transition from an outsourced sewer-cleaning worker to an entrepreneur has brought greater income, stability, self-reliance and social respect.
Sushil Kumar Sharma’s journey demonstrates how financial assistance, capital subsidy and access to modern sanitation equipment can convert occupational experience into sustainable entrepreneurship. His success reflects the role of the NAMASTE–SUY initiative in promoting safety, dignity and economic empowerment among sanitation workers.
Through determination and timely support under NAMASTE–SUY, Sushil has progressed from uncertain outsourced employment to dignified mechanised self-employment. His story is an inspiring example of how targeted assistance can improve livelihoods while advancing safer and more professional sanitation services.

content:
The Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) successfully observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 1st to 15th July, 2026 with active participation from all its Divisions, Attached/Subordinate/Autonomous Organizations including Field Offices located across the country. The fortnight long Pakhwada focused on sanitation, strengthening cleanliness, workplace hygiene, record management, environmental sustainability, waste management and efficient office practices in line with the objectives of Swachh Bharat Mission.
During the fortnight, all the offices and field formations of the Ministry undertook a wide range of activities such as plantation drives, awareness campaigns, seminars, workshops, competitions, rallies, shramdaan and extensive community outreach programmes in Mohallas, schools and public places, Nukkad Nataks, Sea Beach cleaning drives, large scale public participation campaigns, waste-to-wealth initiatives and environmental conservation activities. Initiatives relating to reduction of single-use plastic, waste segregation, recycling and sustainable waste management were undertaken.
The Pakhwada concluded with the Prize Distribution Ceremony of Swachhata Pakhwada Awards–2026 under the chairmanship of the Secretary, MoSPI, wherein Secretary, MoSPI presented Mementos to the three top performing offices. The First, Second and Third Prize was awarded to the Field Operations Division (FOD), National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) and Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) respectively, for their outstanding, exemplary and active participation in the Swachhata Pakhwada.
The Secretary, MoSPI appreciated the active participation and dedicated efforts of all officers and officials across the Ministry. He emphasised that cleanliness may not remain confined only to the Pakhwada but should become an integral part of the working culture and everyday life.
The Ministry reiterates its commitment towards institutionalizing cleanliness, promoting environmental responsibility and fostering a culture of public participation with the vision of a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable India.

title: GOVERNMENT REITERATES ITS COMMITMENT FOR REIMAGINING SKILLING
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
NITI Aayog released a report titled “Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047” which provides a blueprint for a skilling architecture, aligned to the needs of ‘Viksit Bharat’. The report identifies 5 key segments of learners /workforce, including NEET youth in the age group 15-29 years. This is defined as a set of young people who fall under the following categories: (i) Engaged in voluntary work/ household enterprise; (ii) Attending domestic duties; (iii) Not able to work due to health condition; (iv) Spending leisure time; and (v) Others.
In certain sections, the figure of 8.7 crore NEET youth has been misinterpreted as unemployed. The category of NEET in the report refers to those not seeking employment, and the acronym NEET stands for Not in Education, Employment or Training. Therefore, it cannot be read as a measure of joblessness or as an addition to the unemployment rate. The unemployed represent an entirely separate category, drawn from a different population base than that used for the NEET estimate.
The NITI Aayog Report has clearly stated that the database utilised in computation of these figures is based on NSS 78th Round which was collected during the COVID-19 pandemic (FY 2020–21). It was a time of disruption in the field of education and employment and hence the figures stated in the report could be a deviation from the normal trajectory. This is apparent from the fact that the youth NEET percentage is significantly lower in the most recent PLFS round (PLFS 2025).
The government is committed to robust and evidence-based policymaking. As a step to facilitate the same, Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was introduced in 2017-18, ushering in annual estimates in contrast to the earlier regime of NSSO Employment-Unemployment Surveys which were conducted once every five years and hence leaving a trail of considerable lag in actual indices. To further strengthen the evaluation and aligning with international practice, since January 2025, PLFS underwent a further improvement including the shifting of survey period to January-December calendar year cycle.
With a vision to achieve Viksit Bharat@2047, the Government is taking all measures to skill our youth and prepare them for future growth. Hence, even before the publication of the report, the Government has proactively started the implementation of the key reforms suggested in the report through the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. Introduction of the ₹600 crore, Integrated Scheme in Skilling Architecture (ISSA) in the Union Budget 2026–27 as a precursor to the launch of the said report makes the intent of the government amply clear, which is to strengthen convergence across education, skilling, employment, and lifelong learning systems.

title: 5 Years of e-Shram Portal
subtitle: Building an Inclusive Social Security Ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 2:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The e-Shram Portal completes five years on 26 August 2026, marking a significant milestone in strengthening social security for India's unorganised workforce. Launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, it created the country's first-ever Aadhaar-seeded National Database of Unorganised Workers. It gives every registered worker a unique Universal Account Number and has evolved into a one-stop digital platform integrating welfare, jobs, skilling, apprenticeship and pension services. With over 31.89 crore registrations, e-Shram has improved benefit delivery, portability and evidence-based policymaking. It advances the Government's vision of an inclusive, technology-driven social security ecosystem.
Empowering India's Unorganised Workforce
As India advances towards the vision of
Viksit Bharat
, empowering its vast workforce remains central to inclusive and sustainable growth.
The unorganised sector comprises a diverse range of workers, including agricultural labourers, construction workers, domestic workers, street vendors, migrant workers, gig and platform workers, and many others. Together, they form a vital pillar of India’s workforce and economy. Ensuring their access to social security and welfare has therefore remained a key priority of the Government.
Building on this commitment,
the e-Shram Portal was launched on 26 August 2021, and completes 5 years since then.
It marks an important milestone in India's efforts to build a comprehensive social security ecosystem for unorganised workers.
The Vision Behind e-Shram
The e-Shram Portal, developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC), created the country's
first Aadhaar authenticated National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW)
.It provides every registered worker with a unique
12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN)
. The key objectives include:
Improve delivery of social security services by enabling the convergence of welfare schemes across Ministries and Departments.
Facilitate secure sharing of worker data with government agencies through APIs. This supports the effective delivery of welfare schemes and evidence-based policymaking.
Facilitate nationwide access and portability of social security and welfare benefits for migrant and construction workers.
Create a comprehensive national database that supports timely planning and response during national emergencies and crises.
"Unorganised worker" includes a home-based worker, self-employed worker, or a wage worker in the unorganised sector. It also includes a worker in the organised sector who is not a member of ESIC/ EPFO/ Government Employee.
Evolution into a One-Stop Solution
The e-Shram portal transformed from a worker registry into a
unified service delivery platform with the
launch of the
e-Shram One-Stop Solution
on
21 October 2024
. It now integrates
welfare, employment, skilling and pension services.
This aligns with the Union Budget 2024–25 vision of delivering a wide range of labour services through a single digital platform. Registered workers can access eligible schemes and view benefits already received. The platform also promotes convergence across government portals. It strengthens access to social security and improves service delivery for unorganised workers.
The One-Stop Solution brings together
15 Social Security and Welfare Schemes
on a single platform. These include Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-SYM), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC), Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G) and others.
eShram registrants can conveniently enrol in the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) and Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) through the eShram portal. Under PMSBY, workers are eligible for accidental insurance benefits of ₹2 lakh for accidental death or permanent disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability. PMJJBY provides a life insurance cover of ₹2 lakh in the event of death due to any cause.
The portal connects workers with the
National Career Service (NCS)
for employment opportunities. It also provides access to the
Skill India Digital Hub
for skilling and apprenticeship. Workers can also use
myScheme
to identify government schemes for which they may be eligible.
Through the portal, eligible workers can enrol in the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) Scheme, which offers a minimum assured pension of
₹3,000 per month
upon attaining the age of 60 years, subject to eligibility
.
Powered by the
Bhashini
platform, multilingual functionality in 22 languages was introduced in
2025
.
The portal
includes a provision to capture the family details of migrant workers.
It enables
sharing of construction workers' data with States and Union Territories. This facilitates their registration with the respective
Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) Boards
.
eShram provides a platform for the
identification and registration of gig and platform workers
as part of the national database of unorganised workers. As of date, around
11.5 lakh platform workers have registered on the portal
. This database may support the formulation and implementation of suitable social security and welfare measures for such workers.
e-Shram Registration: Eligibility and Process
Registration
on the e-Shram Portal is
simple, accessible
and a
one-time process.
Eligibility
: Any worker aged
16 years and above
, engaged in the unorganised sector, is eligible to register on the e-Shram Portal. A worker must not be an income tax-payer or a member of the
Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)
or the
Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)
.
Coverage
: The portal covers a wide range of unorganised workers. These include construction workers, migrant workers, gig and platform workers, street vendors, domestic workers, agricultural workers, and other unorganised workers.
How to register
: Workers can register by visiting the
e-Shram Portal (
https://register.eshram.gov.in/#/user/self
)
. They can also register through the nearest
Common Service Centre (CSC)
or
State Seva Kendra
. State Government field officers also facilitate registration at the district and sub-district levels.
Registration cost
: Registration on the e-Shram Portal is completely free of cost. Workers are not required to pay any fee to any registering agency or service provider.
Required Documents
: Registration requires their
Aadhaar number (for Aadhar eKYC)
and a
mobile number
(preferably linked with Aadhaar).
Growing Coverage of India's Unorganised Workforce
Registrations on e-Shram portal over the past 5 years reflects broad participation across genders, age groups, occupations and States (as on 18 August, 2026).
Total registrations:
The portal has recorded
31.89 crore
registrations.
Gender distribution:
Women account for
54.28%
of registered workers, while men account for
45.72%
.
Age profile:
0.08% are aged
16-18 years, 55.21%
of registered workers are aged
18–40 years
,
24.18%
are aged
40–50 years
and
20.53%
are above
50 years
(as on 20 August, 2026).
Top occupational categories:
Agriculture, Domestic and Household Workers, Construction, and Apparel account for the highest registrations.
Top States:
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra have recorded the highest registrations.
Mode of registration:
Most registrations have been completed through
Common Service Centres (CSCs)
, followed by
self-registration
.
Building the Future of Labour Welfare
The e-Shram Portal has laid a strong foundation for an inclusive and technology-enabled social security ecosystem for India’s unorganised workforce
. By creating a nationwide digital identity and database for unorganised workers, it has enabled more targeted and transparent delivery of government support. As its coverage and services continue to expand, e-Shram remains an important digital pillar of a more inclusive and future-ready workforce.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported deaths of at least 9 people and 39 others in a critical condition after consuming spurious Indian-Made Foreign Liquor in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat
subtitle:
The Commission issues notices to the Gujarat Chief Secretary and Director General of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The report to include updated status of the death toll, hospitalised victims, investigation, departmental action initiated against erring officers, relief, compensation and medical assistance provided to the families of the deceased and to the survivors

Information also sought on long-term measures to prevent such tragedies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 AUG 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of media reports that at least 9 people died and 39 others were hospitalised in a critical condition after consuming spurious Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat. Reportedly, the illicit liquor was spiked with a high concentration of methanol and was being sold in counterfeit bottles bearing the label of a popular brand. The illicit liquor racket came to light during an investigation of an accidental death case registered for the death of a police recruit.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Gujarat Chief Secretary and Director General of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
The report is expected to include the updated status of the death toll, hospitalised victims and investigation including the steps taken to trace the entire supply chain of methanol and other raw materials. It should also include the details of the departmental action initiated against the suspended police personnel and any other erring officials, relief, compensation and medical assistance provided to the families of the deceased and to the survivors. Besides, the Commission has also sought a report on the long-term measures being implemented to strengthen the enforcement of the prohibition law and prevent such tragedies.
According to the media reports, a large manufacturing setup was uncovered and chemicals, colouring agents, ready-filled counterfeit liquor bottles, fake branded stickers and sticker rolls, bottle caps and cardboard packaging material were seized by police.

content:
The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers today organized the inaugural edition of CHEMCONNECT 2026 at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras on 25th August 2026.
Over 200 leaders, researchers, and entrepreneurs across industry, academia, start-ups, and research institutions, including representatives from the Centres of Excellence established by the Department attended the event.
The inaugural ceremony of the event was attended by Shri Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) as chief guest along with Prof V. Kamakoti, Director of IIT Madras, Dr. G. Venkatesh, Joint Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Prof. Shishir Sinha, Director General, CIPET and Prof. Ethayaraja Mani, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Madras.
Shri Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, inaugurated the event and also launched the Centre of Excellence on Biodegradable Packaging Materials (BioPack) at IIT Madras. The BioPack facility will serve as a hub for sustainable innovation, capacity building, and advanced research in eco-friendly packaging capabilities.
Delivering the inaugural address, Shri Tejveer Singh emphasized the critical role of the chemical sector as a foundational driver feeding into virtually every manufacturing segment of the economy. He highlighted that as India advances toward achieving Viksit Bharat by 2047, strengthening industry-academia partnerships is vital to translate laboratory research into commercially viable products.
The Secretary underscored the imperative of import substitution, noting that goods must be processed domestically to foster greater self-reliance. He expressed confidence that targeted R&D and industry-backed research clusters will expand India's global footprint. Sh. Singh further announced that CHEMCONNECT will become an annual fixture held every July–August to benchmark progress across all the Centres of Excellence.
Speaking on the occasion, Prof. V. Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras, detailed the importance of institutional synergies in taking technology to its logical fruition and assured of full support to the chemical sector through reverse pitching, where industry presents it’s problems to research institutions.
Dr. G. Venkatesh, Joint Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, outlined the vision of the Centre of Excellence scheme, while Prof. Shishir Sinha, Director General, CIPET, highlighted the initiative's alignment with national development goals. Prof. Ethayaraja Mani of IIT Madras, who was the coordinator of the event delivered the welcome address and vote of thanks.
The Secretary, DCPC along with Director IIT Madras also released the compendium of CHEMCONNECT 2026.
